title: What If All of Earth's Water Became One Ball?

scenes.text: What if all the water on Earth formed one ball? It would be smaller than you think.
Oceans, ice caps, lakes, rivers, clouds, even groundwater. Every drop gathered together.
The ball would be about 860 miles across, roughly 1,385 kilometers.
Earth is about 7,900 miles wide, so that ball is only about a ninth of its diameter.
Fresh water, the kind we drink, would be a much tinier ball, under 100 miles across.
The planet that looks blue from space holds a surprisingly small amount of water.

description:
What if all of Earth's water formed one ball?
USGS estimates it would be only about 860 miles across, far smaller than most people guess.
